name: can compose unrelated changes
scenario: composeDesc of '5 0:2' (insert 2 at the end of a 5-length document) then '1 2:0 4' (delete 2 at 1).
expected: String of the composition is '1 2:0 2 0:2'.
class_reason: Pure state values (change descriptions, change sets, Text, selections); no layout, grammar or DOM.
port_notes: Helper `mk(spec)` (mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-change.ts:4-12): repeatedly matches /^(\d+)(?::(\d+))?\s*/ at the start of the remaining string; each match pushes two numbers: +group1 (length) and +group2 when present, else -1 (so "5" is an unchanged span of 5, "0:2" an insertion of 2, "2:0" a deletion of 2, "2:3" a replacement); an empty string gives no sections; a string that does not match makes `exec` return null and the helper throw a TypeError. It builds the value with the protected constructor (`new (ChangeDesc as any)(sections)`), bypassing every check (open question Q5); the same array is obtainable through ChangeDesc.fromJSON. Assertions compare `String(desc)`, i.e. the @internal ChangeDesc.toString format (len or len:ins joined by single spaces), with `ist` (strict ===). Helper `comp(...specs)` (test-change.ts:34-37): pops the last argument as the expected string, maps the rest through `mk`, folds them left to right with `composeDesc`, and asserts `String(result) === expected`. Positions are plain counts; no text, so D1 and D2 do not change any value.

port_notes: Helpers (mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-rangeset.ts:4-59). `Value` (:4-26) extends RangeValue: startSide = spec.startSide ?? 1; endSide = spec.endSide ?? spec.startSide ?? (empty ? 1 : -1); point = empty || !!spec.point; name = spec.name || null; pos = spec.pos ?? null; eq(other) = other instanceof Value && other.name == this.name (no identity shortcut in eq itself; cmpVal adds it). `Value.names(v)` joins, with '/', name or 'POINT' for every value that has a name or is a point (unnamed marks are skipped). `mk(from, to?, spec?)` (:30-34): if `to` is not a number it is the spec and to = from; a string spec means {name: spec}; the value is new Value(spec, from == to) (so an empty range is a point with sides 1/1, a non-empty one a mark with sides 1/-1 unless overridden) and the result is value.range(from, to); every mk call creates a new value object. `mkSet(ranges)` = RangeSet.of(ranges) without sort (:35). `cmp(a, b)` = a.from - b.from, used with Array.prototype.sort (stable) to sort range arrays (:28). `smallRanges` (:46-48): 5000 ranges mk(i, i + 1 + (i % 4), {pos: i}) for i in 0..4999, built once at module load; `set0()` (:49-50) builds mkSet(smallRanges) lazily once and returns the same set object afterwards. `checkSet(set)` (:52-59): set.between(0, set.length, ...) counting calls and asserting from == value.pos when pos is set, then asserting the count equals set.size; `set.length` is @internal (Q5).
